findings.reason: the node would write a test and a behaviour for a widened dispatch scope that the resume path never produces, and its own done-when assertion ("a write scope that is the union of the paths they cite", for a finding outside the fence) would fail against the landed reflex, sending the node to re-open the resume-vs-dispatch decision §12 already settled.
findings.text: §3's deliverable says the reflex composes one repair node "whose write scope is the union of the paths the findings name — declared at dispatch, so a finding outside the reviewed run's fence is granted rather than refused", and its done-when at :146 requires observing "one repair dispatch naming all three, with a write scope that is the union of the paths they cite"; but `dispatch_repair_for_run` never dispatches — every return carries `dispatched: False` (`reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:1034`, :1071) and an unpromoted reviewed run whose worker has exited is repaired by resuming the run itself with the findings as advice, while a promoted run is refused rather than dispatched. A resumed worker runs inside the reviewed run's existing fence, which is exactly why §12 exists to widen that fence for a folded finding and why its Why records the grant being refused there. The scope `repair_write_scope` computes (`reckon/crew/repair.py:392`) is laid into the composed advice, not into a dispatched node's grant, so the out-of-fence grant §3 relies on cannot occur on the only path the reflex takes.

findings.reason: without a stated negative control the node cannot show the guard discriminates, and a hold that never releases passes the measure as written.
findings.text: §6's done-when names no negative control. Every other open section states one explicitly (s3 at :146, s8–s14 each carry "The negative control is executed and logged" or "Negative control."), and §6's only guard case — "a synthetic project whose suite fails at collection holds a tier-none promotion in a test" — demonstrates the hold firing but nothing shows the hold releases when it should not fire (`hold_reason` returns `None` for a passing latest run or a waiver, `reckon/crew/standing_suite.py:515`). A node can satisfy this done-when with a hold that fires on every tier-none promotion.

findings.reason: the section runs in this wave (status `implementable`) and a node carrying three deliverables cannot be reviewed or closed on one verdict; splitting the declaration, the recording and the hold, and dropping the nova clause, changes what the node is.
findings.text: §6 bundles three separable deliverables in one node and one done-when: project configuration declaring its `review.suite` command and budget; the coordinator's wave close running that command once and recording collected/passed/failed/errored counts; and the promotion hold on tiers `none` and `light` while the last run failed to collect or overran its budget. The done-when spans all three ("reckon and nova each declare …; a synthetic project … holds a tier-none promotion in a test; and reckon records at least one standing-suite run …"), so no single verdict closes the node and its gate proves none of the three independently. The rewrite also leaves the nova half of the declaration inside a reckon node's done-when while the closing sentence assigns nova's part to nova's coordinator, so the measure still names a change in another repository as the node's own.

findings.reason: an unmet dependency the plan needs (s7 → s3, s6) is undeclared, so the build order the section states in prose is not enforced anywhere the scheduler reads.
findings.text: §7's done-when reads "§3 closes. §2, §4 and §5 have landed and §6 is met", but the plan declares no `depends-on` for §7: `plan-section-depends-on` carries only `{"s14": ["a-review-is-sized-to-its-risk#s13"]}`, and §7's own `<section data-reckon="section" data-id="s7" … data-links="">` is empty. §7 is status `implementable`, so it is dispatchable as a node, yet nothing in the wiring holds it until §3 has closed and §6 is met — the two open sections it now closes on. The roadmap can schedule the rollup ahead of the sections that define its completion, and a node dispatched to §7 has no deliverable of its own beyond that closure.
